common_name: Navigator III Creeping Red Fescue (A-LIST Improved Shade and Traffic Tolerant Turf Cultivar)

planting.note: Seed into a firm, well-drained bed in early fall at 4-6 lbs per 1,000 sq ft for new seedings, or 2-4 lbs for overseeding; Navigator III is the third generation in Mountain View Seeds' Navigator line of strong creeping red fescue.

directions: Navigator III is the third generation in Mountain View Seeds' Navigator line of strong creeping red fescue, bred to keep the earlier releases' excellent turf quality and drought performance while adding meaningfully better shade tolerance and wear resistance under foot traffic. It carries the A-LIST designation from the Alliance for Low Input Sustainable Turf, reflecting strong trial performance under low-fertility, low-pesticide management where many turf species struggle. Like other fine fescues it forms a fine-bladed, slowly spreading sod best suited to dry shade under trees, naturalized low-mow areas, or blends with other fine fescues and Kentucky bluegrass rather than high-traffic lawns. Seed into a firm, well-drained bed in early fall and keep the surface consistently moist through germination.
sources: Alliance for Low Input Sustainable Turf (A-LIST)

common_name: Sundevil II Bermudagrass (Improved Medium-Dark Green Seeded Turf Cultivar)

planting.note: Broadcast hulled seed at 1-2 lbs per 1,000 square feet once soil is reliably above 65 degrees F; Sundevil II is the improved selection that succeeded the original Sundevil and is now the more widely sold seed source.

directions: Sundevil II is a seeded common-type bermudagrass registered in 2002 as an improvement on the original Sundevil selection, offering growers a seed-propagated alternative to costlier vegetatively-established hybrid bermudagrasses. It forms a uniform, low-growing, medium-dark green stand with a medium-fine blade texture, suited to general-purpose turf use on lawns, sports fields, and fairways. Sow into a firm, weed-free seedbed in late spring once soil is reliably warm, water lightly and frequently until germination, and expect the typical drought tolerance, full-sun requirement, and winter dormancy common to all seeded bermudagrass. Mow regularly during the growing season to maintain a dense, even canopy.
sources: Jacklin Seed / Simplot — Sundevil II Bermudagrass
Crop Science journal registration (Samudio et al., 2002)
